title: Quantum Internet in the Sky: Vision, Challenges, Solutions, and Future Directions
venue: IEEE Communications Magazine, vol. 62, no. 10, 2024 (magazine), DOI 10.1109/MCOM.003.2300835
description: A question counts as answered at rank r if the r-th retrieved chunk contains ANY of its evidence phrases (case and whitespace insensitive). Evidence phrases are copied from the PDF's own text, not from the parser output, so text lost by the parser shows up as a miss. Questions with no evidence are not answered by the paper; they are used to choose the relevance threshold.

questions.question: At what altitudes do high-altitude platform stations operate?
evidence: altitudes ranging from 19 km to 22 km

questions.question: Why can drones only act as temporary quantum relays?
evidence: the trade-off between the payload-carrying capacity and the operational time

questions.question: What can beam wandering do to an uplink towards a satellite?
evidence: can cause the uplink beam to miss the target satellite

questions.question: How long a secret key is reached at the end of the satellite pass with weak pointing errors?
What entanglement fidelity can a narrow transmit beam keep even in daytime?
Which optical wavelength copes better with atmospheric turbulence on the satellite-to-ground link?
evidence: the 1550-nm wavelength is more resilient against turbulence

questions.question: How much classical information can a single eight-level qudit carry?
evidence: 3 bits of classical information can be encoded using only one quantum state

questions.question: What is the payload weight limit for a HAPS quantum terminal?
evidence: a total payload weighing less than 70 kg
